newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF rises strongly on sale hopes.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF rises strongly on sale hopes.

text.p: Shares in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF led the risers on the Paris Bourse on Thursday after Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the state could cut its stake to below 50 percent from 58 percent now.
At 0847 GMT, Thomson-CSF was up 4.83 percent at 169.40 francs while the blue-chip index was up 0.16 percent.

Strauss-Kahn told a parliamentary commission on Wednesday that no decisions had been taken on the future of Europe's top defence electronics supplier, whose planned privatisation was abandoned on Friday.

But he gave the first cabinet indication that the Socialist-led government was considering letting its 58 percent stake drop below half way to allow private partners a role in fending off tough competition from the United States.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Friday cancelled plans by his centre-right predecessors to sell the state's 58 percent stake. His office said a new project to muster a French defence electronics group around a "decisive" public share in Thomson-CSF would be launched soon, but gave no details.

French newspapers have speculated this would involve the government dropping its participation in Thomson-CSF to 40 percent, perhaps as little as 33 percent, by bringing in new capital but without selling off any public stock directly.
